title: Papa Lightfoot and the harmonica players Johnny Benson and Slim
summary: Marquez asks about harmonica player Papa Lightfoot; Longhair cannot place him and thinks of Johnny Benson, who played harmonica and drank a lot of wine.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: You got anything else to say? Let me just put it down here. What do I want to say? One thing I wanted to ask you too is, you know Papa Lightfoot? Harmonica player? Alexander Lightfoot?
We always called him Papa Lightfoot.
I'm trying to think of where I know him from.
He made, he cut two records down here for Aladdin in like 1954, 1953. He did Saints Go Marching In and Wine, Women and Whiskey. That's two things he did down here.

He didn't sound to me. I'm sure, I'm not positive, but I'm sure I know him. Like I said, man, you can get so clattered up by mixing and doing so many different things. You know exactly what one person does and what the other one don't do. Like I got confused with him. He really looked for me.
About stuff like stuff I haven't met him.
If that's the same fellow, you know who I think that is, Alan? Listening to their voice. Remember Johnny Benson? Benson played harmonica all around.
I think he said he'd go by the name of Slim. Hoppo.
One that had his forehead had him?
Yeah. He drank so much wine.
